newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields fall, crown firms on Riksbank.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields fall, crown firms on Riksbank.

text.p: Swedish bonds yields fell and the crown firmed on Thursday after the Riksbank released its latest quarterly inflation report, cutting its inflation forecast to 0.5 percent in 1997 from an earlier 1.5 percent.

"It is the downgrading of the Riksbank's inflation forecast that made short yields fall and that also made the crown go stronger," a trader said. He added it was positive that the crown closed below 4.55 against the mark.
The crown firmed to 4.5370 against the mark, from 4.5600 late on Wednesday, after being highly volatile and soft in the past week.
The crown also benefited from a report by an investment bank that said the currency was undervalued, dealers said.
The six-month T-bill rate fell seven basis points to 4.24 percent and the ten-year bond yield dropped eight basis points to 7.40 percent.
Bond yields were also supported by stronger markets in Italy and Spain, dealers said.
But the market was volatile and dealers said it could well remain so until the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on March 25.
